accuracy.evidence: Mechanism checked against Chemguide's free-radical substitution pages: initiation Cl₂ → 2Cl• by UV homolytic fission; propagation Cl• + CH₄ → HCl + •CH₃ and •CH₃ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + Cl•; termination giving Cl₂, CH₃Cl or C₂H₆; further substitution to CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄. Mean bond enthalpies Cl–Cl ≈ 242 and C–H ≈ 413 kJ/mol are the standard A-level data values. Stoichiometry (n CH₄ → 4n HCl for CCl₄, 3n Cl₂ for CHCl₃, 2n + 2 H in CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, 6 − k H left on ethane) was checked for every parameter corner. The mixture simulation is a stated simplification (each C–H equally likely to be hit), which gives the right trends: 1 : 10 Cl₂ : CH₄ gives ~100% CH₃Cl, 1 : 1 a four-product mixture, 4 : 1 all CCl₄.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips examiners report for this mechanism: H₂ instead of HCl as the second product (challenge 'h2', mastery m8), UV breaking C–H instead of Cl–Cl (prediction 1, CQ 'ch', tapping methane in the flask gives 'C–H is too strong'), Cl• taking a whole CH₃ group or forming Cl⁻ (prediction 2), confusing initiation, propagation and termination (CQ 'init'/'term', sorter visual), expecting only CH₃Cl from a 1 : 1 mix (prediction 4), and using excess chlorine to get CH₃Cl ('xs').

lab_distinct.evidence: Built for this mechanism: a dark/UV flask where only Cl₂ splits on tap, a two-target propagation loop where the learner must hit CH₄ then Cl₂ (wrong target explained) with a chain-cycle counter, a radical tray that pairs any two radicals into the three termination products, and a Cl₂ : CH₄ ratio simulation whose product bars the learner steers to ≥85% CH₃Cl. gate_lab_distinct passes; none of this appears in the alkane, halogen or functional-group labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea comes from the learner's action first: tapping in the dark does nothing and tapping methane in UV does nothing, so only Cl–Cl breaks; three loops show the radical coming back; pairing radicals shows why the chain stops and where ethane comes from; running 1 : 1 shows all four chloromethanes; and lowering the chlorine until CH₃Cl passes 85% shows why excess methane is used. The completion text then names initiation, propagation, termination and further substitution.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: 'C–H in methane' for what UV breaks, 'the whole CH₃ group' for what Cl• takes, and 'Only CH₃Cl and HCl' for the 1 : 1 product, which is what the overall equation suggests. Each is contradicted by the task that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The challenge alternates generated 'substituted k times' product questions (wrong options: H₂ instead of HCl, HCl missing) with five concept questions on UV, propagation, mixtures, excess methane and the meaning of substitution. Every distractor has its own message naming the slip (e.g. 'C–H is 413 kJ/mol; Cl–Cl is only 242…', 'That is cracking…'), and the balanced equation is shown after each product question.

readability.evidence: Learner text reads at FK grade 3.1 and adult text at 7.4, inside the 6.5 and 9.5 limits. 'Substitution' and 'radical' are defined in plain words before use, and canvas headings are one-line states such as 'Step 1: a Cl• radical meets CH₄' and 'Cl₂ : CH₄ = 1 : 1'.

no_filler.evidence: Each paragraph adds a stage of the mechanism, the reason for UV, the mixture or how to steer it; the adult text lists the mistakes and the half-headed arrow point. Lab copy is limited to instructions, live counts and feedback; there is no scene-setting or praise text.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of every step after Show me in dark and light themes: the UV lamp sits in the header clear of the four methane molecules, split Cl• pairs are offset diagonally so neighbours do not merge, propagation equations fit on one line, product bars and their counts sit under the result pill, and all controls are 44 px buttons that wrap.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: UV lamp on/off, Split next Cl₂, Hit CH₄ / Hit Cl₂, one button per radical pair, Less/More Cl₂ and Run. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the radicals made, chain cycles, termination products or full product counts and CH₃Cl percentage, and walk.cjs reports axe clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
